questions.q: 'What he promised was never delivered.' — clause type?
questions.a: Noun clause — 'what he promised' is the subject; swap in 'It' and the sentence stands. A wrong answer 'adjective clause' shows connector-based classification instead of function-based.

questions.q: 'The house that Jack built is old.' — is 'that Jack built' a noun clause?
questions.a: No — adjective/relative clause; it describes 'house' (which house? that Jack built). 'That' here replaces 'which' and refers to the noun — not a content clause. The same connector, different job.

questions.q: 'She left because the meeting ended.' — clause type and its question?
questions.a: Adverb clause of reason — it answers 'why did she leave?' about the main verb. A wrong answer 'noun clause' shows the student didn't test what the clause modifies.

questions.q: ______ clauses are classified by the JOB they do in the main clause: a noun clause works as subject/object/complement ('What he said was true'), an adjective (relative) clause describes a noun ('the book that I bought'), an adverb clause modifies the verb for time/reason/condition ('when she arrived').

Fill in the blank: The substitution tests: noun clause — replace it with 'something/it' and the ______ survives ('What he said' → 'It was true').
What is Subordinate clauses? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Subordinate clauses are classified by the JOB they do in the main clause: a noun clause works as subject/object/complement ('What he said was true'), an adjective (relative) clause describes a noun ('the book that I bought'), an adverb clause modifies the verb for time/reason/condition ('when she arrived').

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Subordinate clauses?
questions.a: Students classify clauses by their introductory word — assuming every 'that'-clause is a noun clause and every 'when'-clause is adverbial — instead of asking what job the clause performs in its sentence.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student identifies the clause type by its grammatical function — not by its connector — and distinguishes 'that'-noun-clauses from 'that'-relative-clauses.
